title: fix(scenarios): asked-back:asks reads a request phrase after a clause mark
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLW6dHPW6sSheA32XPKZzPV)_
Fixes #35058
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：场景评测 asked-back 的「是否在反问」检查（`asked-back:asks`）现在也认逗号、分号、冒号（全角半角都算）后面的请求短语，例如「我不替你选，请确认你要哪一个：」；asked-back 规则版本从 rev 2 升到 rev 3，记分卡显示 `asked-back rev 3`。
- **为什么改**：ask 技能迭代第 6 轮里，`dq_travel_spend` 第 3 次回答其实正确地反问了，却因为「请确认」跟在逗号后、又没有问号，被判成「没有问用户任何问题」，datasets 只拿到 24/25。
- **风险与回滚**：只影响评测打分（`@objectstack/scenarios`），不影响运行时。rev 2 与 rev 3 的轮次不能直接对比，记分卡上的版本号会区分它们。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-dataset-grade.ts`（`REQUEST_PHRASE` / `ASKS` 两处正则，以及 `DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS` 改成 3）、`packages/qa/scenarios/test/score/scenario-dataset-grade.test.ts`（新的 `asked-back:asks` describe）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/score/scenario-dataset-grade.test.ts`，预期 26 个测试全过，其中包括第 6 轮第 3 次回答的原文。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- `asked-back:asks` (`ASKS` in `scenario-dataset-grade.ts`): a request phrase (`please confirm` / `clarify` / `specify` / `tell me` / `let me know`, `could you clarify` / `confirm` / `specify`, 请确认, 请说明, 请告诉我, 请明确, 您是指, 你是指) now asks when it opens a **clause**, after `,` `，` `;` `；` `:` `：`. Before, it counted only at the start of the text, a line, or a sentence (after `.` `。` `!` `！`). The question-mark path and the phrase list did not change.
- **Why the anchor stays, and what it still protects.** The anchor came in with the grader itself (#34808, "at a line's or sentence's start"). #34997 and #35023 did not touch it. It keeps two kinds of text from counting as an ask:
  - A phrase inside a clause, either quoted (「点“请确认”提交」) or reported (`I asked finance to please confirm the totals`). The phrase still has to open its clause. Opening quotes and plain words are not boundaries, so both still fail `asks`.
  - `which one` / `which of`. This keeps the sentence-only anchor. After a comma it is usually a relative clause (`…, which of course differ`, `…, which one team maintains`), and a real question spelled that way ends in a question mark, which the `?` path already reads.
- The phrase list moved into its own constant (`REQUEST_PHRASE`), so the two anchors share one list.
- **Revision.** The same recording now grades differently, so `DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS['asked-back']` goes from 2 to 3. I followed #35023: a line in the table's doc block, and the `Run · datasets` row now reads `asked-back rev 3 k/N` (the scorecard code did not change, it reads the table). README: the `asked-back` entry now says what counts as an ask, and "`asked-back` is at 3".
- Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/scenarios`. No export was added, removed or changed shape (`DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS` keeps its type, and only its value moves), so `Clause-②: no`.

## Tests

All readings are at head `5f12a0c23`.

- New top-level `describe` in `test/score/scenario-dataset-grade.test.ts`, graded against `travel_expense` `dq_travel_spend` (the travel card loader moved to module scope so both travel describes share it):
  - **(1) positive:** the iteration 6 rep 3 reply, verbatim. The whole grade passes (`asks`, `names-candidates`, `no-figure`) at `revision` 3. Clause-mark variants in both widths and both languages also pass (`，请确认`, `；请说明`, `： 您是指`, `, please confirm`, `; could you clarify`, `: please let me know`).
  - **(2) negative:** a figure-bearing reply still fails, with only `asked-back:no-figure` failing. One case is the recorded reply plus 「目前报销金额合计 10,290 元。」, and the other is 「报销金额合计 10,290 元，请确认…」. Both read `[10290]`.
  - **(3) what the anchor protects:** a quoted 「“请确认”」, a reported `to please confirm`, and `, which of course differ` / `, which one team maintains` each fail only `asked-back:asks`.
- The existing recorded-reply pin now expects `revision` 3 instead of 2.

<details><summary>Package suite, typecheck, ablation</summary>

- Merged head `5f12a0c23`, run under the verification lock: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/scenarios...' build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios test`. Exit 0. `Test Files 39 passed (39)`, `Tests 1120 passed (1120)`. `tsc --listFiles` includes the edited test file.
- Ablation, done once with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` at `468dc95f0`. The tests import `src/`, so there is no dist leg. The mutation put the old sentence-only anchor back on `REQUEST_PHRASE`. The tool reported "anchor x1 -> x0, replace x0 -> x1, blob 76317b6c -> c28725a5". Result: `Tests 3 failed | 23 passed (26)`. The recorded-reply pin (1) fails, and so do the clause-mark variants and the second negative case (its 请确认 follows a comma, so `asks` fails there too). After the restore, the blob matched HEAD (`76317b6c`) and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Wider than before, on purpose:** a conditional offer after a comma now counts as asking. Example: iteration 0 `dq_claimed_so_far` rep 1, 「如果"claim"指的是其他对象…，请告诉我，我再查。」. That grade still fails, on `names-candidates` and `no-figure`. An ask-back passes only when it also names every candidate and states no figure, so a reply that answers cannot pass through this widening.
- Still not an ask: a request phrase after any other mark (`、`, a dash, a closing quote), and `which one` after a comma with no question mark.
- The replays below ran on this checkout's workspace packages. Their `Seed` reads `757/757` and `Run-问数` reads `25/65` (iteration 3 and 5: `24/65`). The loop's own regrades (`regrade-rev2/`) read `173/757 · 584 refused` and `25/25 · 40 not measured`. The seed difference comes from the build the packages are packed from, not from this diff, which touches only the dataset grader. The datasets row does not read the seed.

## Verification

| Iteration | main (rev 2, the loop's regrade) | this branch (rev 3) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 6 | `24/25 (metric-selected 10/10 · asked-back rev 2 9/10 · fallback-labelled 5/5)` | `25/25 (metric-selected 10/10 · asked-back rev 3 10/10 · fallback-labelled 5/5)` |
| 5 | `25/25 (… asked-back rev 2 10/10 …)` | `25/25 (metric-selected 10/10 · asked-back rev 3 10/10 · fallback-labelled 5/5)` |

| 0 | `19/25 (metric-selected 10/10 · asked-back rev 2 5/10 · fallback-labelled 4/5)` | `19/25 (metric-selected 10/10 · asked-back rev 3 5/10 · fallback-labelled 4/5)` |

- Iterations 0 to 5 ran at `468dc95f0`, the fix before the merge of origin/main. Iteration 6 ran twice: once at `468dc95f0` and again at the merged head `5f12a0c23`, after origin/main brought in #35064 (`driver.ts`). Both runs read the row shown.
- The only grade that changed is iteration 6 `dq_travel_spend` rep 3, which went from fail to pass. As a cross-check, I graded every recorded dataset turn directly, outside the runner, with this branch's grader and with base `eb7b09d4`'s grader. Every iteration matched the table. Per check, one other result moved: iteration 0 `dq_claimed_so_far` rep 1 now passes `asks` but still fails `names-candidates` and `no-figure` (see Acceptance notes). No ask-back went the wrong way.

</details>

<details><summary>Local gates</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `5f12a0c23` derived 60 commands. Each was run, and its exit code was captured before any pipe. 59 exited 0. One exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), so it is NOT MEASURED: `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`. Its positive-control fixture is pinned to a commit this clone cannot reach ("Deepen the clone: git fetch --unshallow origin main"), and it tests the checker itself, which this diff does not touch.
- `--ran` reconciliation: `60 derived, 59 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with every line carrying its exit code.
- `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs`: `VERDICT clean exit 0`. It merges cleanly with origin/main and with #35044, which shares `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`.
- CI families are left to this PR's check-runs.

</details>
